why: The reply says none of the available Magic Hour tools can crop or reframe a video to a new aspect ratio. It called no tool and gives a manual ffmpeg workaround. It offers to try an AI edit only as a secondary option, so the main classification is cannot.
text:
I didn't run anything, because none of the Magic Hour tools I have can do this. None of them can crop or reframe a video to a new aspect ratio:
- The video editor (edit_video) only takes a text prompt. It has no aspect-ratio setting, so the output stays the same shape as your clip. It also redraws every frame with AI, which can change her face and the details. That is not what you want from a plain crop, and it would use credits for nothing.
- The other video tools (restyle, upscale, subtitles, translate, lip sync, face swap) all keep the original frame shape too.

A plain center crop is a simple job you can do free on your own computer, and it keeps the sound exactly as it is. With ffmpeg:

ffmpeg -i talk-one.mp4 -vf "crop=ih*9/16:ih,scale=1080:1920" -c:a copy talk-one-vertical.mp4

- This cuts a 9:16 slice from the center of the frame, so she stays in the middle if she's centered now.
- It keeps the whole 10 seconds and copies the audio as is. It adds no captions.
- If she's a bit off-center, change it to crop=ih*9/16:ih:X:0, where X is how many pixels from the left edge the crop starts.
- If you'd rather not use a command line, CapCut, iMovie and the free Clipchamp editor all have a "9:16" or "crop" option that does the same thing.

If you still want me to try an AI edit in Magic Hour, I can. But the result would still be horizontal and her look might change, so I don't recommend it.
